reconcile.note: Gill equates Ishvi with Abinadab as one son under two names and notes Eshbaal is omitted from 1 Samuel 14:49 because only the sons slain in battle are named there.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain numeric and name clash between the three sons named in 1 Samuel 14:49 and the four sons listed in 1 Chronicles 8:33.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishvi, and Malchishua
sides.verseText: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishvi, and Malchishua; and the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:

sides.snippet: Saul became the father of Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal
sides.verseText: Ner became the father of Kish; and Kish became the father of Saul; and Saul became the father of Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
